analysis: The supplied units are CHANGELOG.md text excerpts (head side, starting at lines 392 and 617). They are documentation only: no executable code, config, or permission changes appear in the visible hunks. The entries describe App Attest recovery/retry (v0.9.8 and later), MDM-optional authorization, SSD prefix-cache defaults, cache write priority and the disk budget, Bonsai SSD-cache eligibility, and coordinator hot-path changes. They are consistent with the existing threat model (T-041 SSD tier posture, T-052..T-058 App Attest authorization, TB-011). One discrepancy to flag for the next pass: the T-041 definition (sliding TTL of 30 minutes since 2026-09-26) is not contradicted by the changelog excerpts, but a changelog line cannot confirm the actual code. Nothing in this PR text alters trust assumptions, so no finding is raised. Claimed code behaviors (retry cadences of 1/5/10 minutes not extending grants, atomic base-reward commits, fencing of revoked credentials) live in files not supplied here. Coverage is limited to the documentation excerpts, so the real source changes in this PR (if any) must be examined in other units. Citing the SSD cache excerpt: default eligibility for Bonsai 2 and the 'Unreleased' SSD checkpoint entries mention a 100 GiB ceiling and a resident cache opt-in (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY). These are historical entries superseded by later entries, so they are not a new regression.
